items.title: Christopher "Happy" Goldston Interview, 1959-01-13
items.q: Yeah, he was a drummer. He was a good drummer.

ctx.x: Bill Matthews used to play drums too, didn't he?
Yeah, he was a drummer. He was a good drummer. He was a good drummer. Which all them masters were good drummers.
Were there any other good drummers up here uptown? Did you ever hear of Walder Brundy? Do you remember?

items.title: Bill Matthews Interview, 1959-03-10
items.q: So, and things was really dead, dead, dead, me and Happy. We stuck with Celestine.

ctx.x: Did the Shots Madison ever play on the records with you in the old days? Ricard. Shots. You know, Shots. Kid Schatz Madison. All you talking about Shots? Shots. Oh, sure. Was he on the records?

Not with me. Not on the records. Shots never didn't leave Ricard. Shots was stuck with Ricard. He stayed with Ricard. Shots and this boy, uh, but this boy, uh, played trombone. Well, they all stuck with Ricard. Yeah. David Jones and them, they stayed on the Pelican with Ricard. Emma Barris, all them John Porter, they all stayed with Ricard on the Pelican. Yeah. Papa Celestine and David Ricard fell out for one dollar. Really? That's right. That's why they made the split. They won one large dollar. That's why they…

And the next six months Celestine had taken the job over from Ricard. And that threw at Ricard and made everything go to Papa Celestine. You see? Everything was Papa Celestine. So Papa Celestine was sick then. I know he was very sick then. So he worked there a few years and got himself straightened out. And he stopped to fool him around. He didn't want to work anymore, you know. Didn't know how to quit. So finally he jumped down. So Houston, he burst a little to the board. Houston said, what do you want to do? He…
